provenance.notes: IMPORTANT, real-hardware confirmed 2026-07-21: this camera's on-screen settings display does NOT live-update after a video_format write — the change genuinely takes effect (confirmed both by the wire and by power-cycling the camera, which then shows the new value) — but the body's menu keeps showing the OLD value until rebooted. Do not treat a static on-screen display alone as evidence a write failed; check tools/captures/ or power-cycle to confirm. dimension_enum values found so far match POCKET_6K_G2_v7.9's numbers exactly for every resolution tested (independently confirmed on this camera's own captures, not copied — see the resolutions table below) — 0x02 also produced a transition to the same pixel dimensions as 0x13 ('6K') once, but with fps clamped to 30 instead of the requested 50 and no confirming echo on a repeat attempt; recorded as an open, unresolved candidate rather than a second dimension_enums entry (the schema only holds one enum per resolution/codec pair) — see the '6K' resolution entry's own comment.

provenance.notes:
category/parameter directly observed on the wire. data_type/reserved for WRITES mirror the G2's convention (its own reports use data_type 0x02, not the claimed write byte 0x82 — same discrepancy documented for the G2, docs/settings.md §3). The 2026-07-22 --repeat 2 send (real change: 2.8K 17:9/50fps -> 4K DCI/25fps, BRAW 8:1 unchanged) confirmed a genuine write+echo cycle for the first time — TX matched, and the echoed (fps_int, width, height, frame_flags)=(25, 4096, 2160, 0x10) matched both the request and fps_modes."25" exactly, though timing was ambiguous (see docs/settings.md §15): the echo arrived right as send 2 was issued, meaning it was send 1's own report delivered after send 1's capture window had already closed (the lens-metadata burst on category 0x0C has repeatedly dominated recent capture windows on this camera and delayed genuine settings echoes past their window) — not proof send 2 (redundant) echoed on its own. No second/fresh 0x01/0x09 report appeared anywhere in send 2's window, consistent with the same no-echo-on-redundant-write behavior already confirmed for this family via the G2 and via codec_quality here.

KNOWN LIMITATION, real-hardware confirmed 2026-07-22 (see docs/settings.md §16): set_recording_format cannot retarget resolution to 4K DCI while ProRes is the active codec family, on this camera. Two independent examples/change_codec.py runs (echo_timeout_s=6.0, ruling out the earlier lens-burst timing false-negative) targeted ProRes 422/4K DCI/25 starting from a genuinely different prior resolution (5.7K 17:9/60fps and 4K DCI-under-BRAW/25fps respectively). In both runs set_video_format's proxy write to (UHD, ProRes) and the follow-up set_codec_quality write to ProRes/422 both landed and echoed cleanly and promptly (confirmed by a fresh 0x01/0x09 report showing width=3840/UHD and a fresh 0x0A/0x00 report showing codec_id=2/variant_id=1) — so the camera was unambiguously in ProRes/422/UHD, not still mid-transition, when the final set_recording_format(4K DCI, 25) write went out. That write then produced zero fresh 0x01/0x09 reports over the full 6.0s window in both runs — only one stale duplicate of the prior UHD report (width=3840, byte-identical to the pre-write report) plus the ambient 0x09/0x00 storage telemetry that free-runs regardless of any write, so BMDVerificationError was raised both times. The identical target reached via BRAW instead (dimension_enums.BRAW=8 for 4K DCI) succeeds every time in the same script run, in one step, via set_video_format alone — recording_format's retarget step is never even needed for BRAW. A third, superficially similar zero-echo result (an isolated tools/control/send_settings_command.py --packet recording_format --resolution "4K DCI" --fps 25 run) turned out NOT to be independent evidence: at the time it ran, the camera was already at BRAW/5:1/4K DCI/25fps/frame_flags=0x10 from the preceding change_codec.py run's own successful BRAW combo — an exact byte-for-byte match of the requested write, so its silence is fully explained by the already-confirmed redundant-write no-echo behavior, not by this ProRes-specific limitation. This makes the PRO's ProRes/4K DCI gap worse than the G2's: the G2's documented two-step proxy workaround (video_format to a reachable resolution, then recording_format to nudge the rest of the way) is known to actually reach 4K DCI/ProRes on that camera (docs/settings.md §7-§9); on the PRO, the same workaround's second step never confirms. set_camera_format() has no PRO-specific handling for this yet — a caller requesting (ProRes, 4K DCI) on this camera should currently expect a BMDVerificationError from the recording_format step, not a successful write.

4K DCI._comment: Camera offers 4K DCI under both codecs (operator-confirmed), but the only known dimension_enum (8) reaches BRAW's 4K DCI only — same unresolved gap as POCKET_6K_G2_v7.9's 4K DCI/ProRes (docs/settings.md §7-§9), independently observed here, not assumed from the G2. Unlike the G2, the two-step proxy workaround (video_format to UHD, then recording_format to nudge to 4K DCI) does NOT close this gap on the PRO: two real-hardware examples/change_codec.py round trips (2026-07-22, docs/settings.md §16) confirmed video_format+codec_quality land ProRes/422/UHD cleanly, then recording_format's write to 4K DCI gets no echo at all within 6.0s. See commands.recording_format's provenance for the full evidence. ProRes/4K DCI is currently unreachable on this camera via CameraSession.

provenance.method: passive observation from examples/record_start_stop.py real-hardware logs during induced SD card slow-write-speed testing
provenance.notes: Raw bytes FF 07 00 00 09 01 01 02 00 FE 00. Payload byte at offset 1 flips 0x01 (nominal) -> 0xFE (-2, low_margin) 0.1-1.4s before every autonomous unexpected stop observed on a known-slow SD card — 6/6 occurrences, 3 cycles x 2 camera models (POCKET_6K_G2 v7.9, POCKET_6K_PRO v8.6). Never -2 in 7 unrelated normal-session logs, where this notification fires once per session and stays 0x01. Payload offsets 0 and 2 are constant (0x00) in every sample, both conditions. NOT yet isolated from other possible autostop causes (card full, card removed, power loss) — 'slow write speed' is inference from test context, not read off the wire alone. See docs/recording.md's 'Camera-initiated stop detection' section.
